title: Number of Sub-arrays With Odd Sum
statement: Count the non-empty contiguous subarrays of the integer array `arr` whose elements add up to an odd number. Subarrays taken from different positions count separately, even when they hold the same values. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Summing every subarray works but takes O(n²). Instead, think of prefix sums: the subarray that ends at index `j` and starts after prefix `i` has sum `prefix[j] - prefix[i]`, which is odd exactly when the two prefixes have different parity. So for each end position we only need to know how many earlier prefixes were even and how many were odd. The empty prefix (sum 0) counts as one even prefix.

## Approach

1. Start with `evenPrefixes = 1` (the empty prefix), `oddPrefixes = 0`, `parity = 0` and `count = 0`.
2. For each `value`, update `parity`, the parity of the running prefix sum.
3. If `parity` is odd, every earlier even prefix pairs with it to form an odd subarray: add `evenPrefixes` to `count`, then increment `oddPrefixes`.
4. If it is even, add `oddPrefixes` instead and increment `evenPrefixes`.
5. Return `count`, kept below `MOD` along the way.

## Example 1, step by step

For `arr = [1, 3, 5]`:

- `value = 1`: `parity = 1`; add `evenPrefixes = 1`, so `count = 1`; `oddPrefixes = 1`.
- `value = 3`: `parity = 0`; add `oddPrefixes = 1`, so `count = 2`; `evenPrefixes = 2`.
- `value = 5`: `parity = 1`; add `evenPrefixes = 2`, so `count = 4`; `oddPrefixes = 2`.

The answer is 4: the subarrays `[1]`, `[3]`, `[5]` and `[1, 3, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1): only two counters and the running parity.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the empty prefix (`evenPrefixes = 1`) misses every odd subarray that starts at index 0.
- Add the matching count before incrementing the counter for the current prefix, or a prefix pairs with itself.
- The count can exceed 10^9 + 7 for long arrays; reduce as you go (and use a 64-bit or modded counter in Java and C).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus 10^9 + 7 |
| `evenPrefixes`, `oddPrefixes` | how many prefixes so far had an even or an odd sum |
| `parity` | parity of the current prefix sum (0 or 1) |
| `count` | odd-sum subarrays found so far |

narration.3: The empty prefix has sum 0, so one even prefix exists before any element.
narration.4: No odd prefix has been seen yet.
narration.8: Visit each element; it ends a new prefix and a new set of subarrays.
narration.9: Only the prefix sum's parity matters, so keep just that.
narration.10: An odd prefix forms an odd subarray with every earlier even prefix.
narration.11: Add those even prefixes to the count.
narration.12: This prefix becomes another odd prefix for later ends.
narration.14: An even prefix pairs with every earlier odd prefix instead.
narration.15: Record this even prefix for later ends.
narration.18: Every subarray end was counted exactly once.
